correctness.rationale: For each comparable \(x\leq y\), persistence gives \(R(y)\subseteq R(x)\). Any schema countervaluation can be reduced to an upset \(U\); the only way for \(y\) to satisfy \(\Box p\) while \(x\) does not is \(R(x)\not\subseteq\uparrow R(y)\). Choosing \(U=\uparrow R(y)\) proves necessity, and upward closure of every formula truth set proves sufficiency. Common row minima on a finite chain yield the exact cutoff count; a two-world witness verifies the sharp strictness of the weaker condition. The packaged checker exhaustively compares the original semantic clauses for all posets through \(n=3\) and counts chains through \(n=4\); computation is not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The source motivates a precise structural gap: its canonical sufficient BEM condition is stronger than actual validity. The theorem answers that gap at arbitrary cardinality by one first-order condition, reduces the full schema to a single atomic instance, and completely enumerates the natural finite-chain family, including a sharp two-world strict witness. These are reusable semantical classification and quantitative invariants rather than a mere presentation of the known four-world counterexample.
